clue.text: Extensive coverage of performance in The Ring

definitions.text: Extensive coverage of performance in The Ring

parts.words: Extensive coverage of performance in The Ring
parts.note: a huge canvas covering the ring where a circus performs, not Wagner's opera cycle

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' suggests Wagner's operas; it is the circus ring, covered by the large tent.
explanation.definitionFit: The main circus tent is a vast canvas roof stretched over the performing ring.

clue.text: Lament extinct, mountain-dwelling bird

indicators.note: the bird lives inside the mountain word, so its letters sit within it

parts.note: BEN is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis
the moa was a huge flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct

explanation.surface: Someone mourns a vanished bird that once lived high in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extinct' describes the bird: the moa died out centuries ago.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan is to grieve over or complain about, a synonym of lament as a verb.

clue.text: Winger scored goal, not centre, curling to back of net

indicators.note: the letters bend and twist into a new order, as a curling shot does
the goal word loses its middle letters, keeping only its outside pair
the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A footballer's shot is described curling into the back of the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curling' rearranges SCORED with GL (goal without its middle OA) to give GOLDCRES; 'back of' adds T from net. 'Winger' looks like a footballer but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger is any creature with wings; the goldcrest is Britain's smallest songbird.

clue.text: Drinking spirits in the bar, you'll get it in the neck!

definitions.text: Drinking spirits in the bar, you'll get it in the neck!

parts.words: Drinking spirits in the bar, you'll get it in the neck!
parts.note: a pub measuring device fixed into the upturned neck of a spirits bottle, with the idiom 'get it in the neck' meaning to be punished

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a warning about drinking; in a British pub, spirits are poured through a measure fitted into the bottle's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar measure fitted to an inverted bottle dispenses a fixed shot of spirits.

clue.text: . Expenses mostly sky-high?

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a business's running costs are its overheads

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether business costs have gone through the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading full stop is a printing stray. 'mostly' trims the final S from OVERHEADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something above one's head, up in the sky, is sky-high in the literal sense.

clue.text: Where parallels may be drawn with a meeting, apparently

definitions.text: Where parallels may be drawn with a meeting, apparently

parts.words: Where parallels may be drawn with a meeting, apparently
parts.note: in perspective drawing, parallel lines are drawn so they seem to converge at a single spot on the horizon

explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing parallels' suggests making comparisons; here it is literal drawing of parallel lines.
explanation.definitionFit: In perspective art, receding parallel lines appear to meet at this point on the horizon.

clue.text: Italian telling votes against outstanding feature

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian, from Rome

indicators.note: telling means saying aloud, so the votes word is heard, not seen

parts.note: in Parliament the votes against are the noes

explanation.surface: An Italian is reporting the votes cast against a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' means sticking out: a hooked nose with a prominent bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent aquiline nose literally stands out from the face, a feature that projects.

clue.text: A girl named Heather

definitions.meaning: the botanical genus of heaths and heathers

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a female first name and the Latin genus name of the heather plants.

clue.text: Took action, calling in the engineers, or was vacillating?

indicators.note: the engineers are summoned into the middle of the action word

parts.note: took action means did something
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether calling out the engineers was decisive or indecisive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling in the engineers' reads as summoning help, but 'calling in' is the container signal; RE (Royal Engineers) is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to hesitate indecisively, the same as vacillating.

clue.text: Comment on unexpected appearance of Nick's address?

definitions.meaning: a remark made when someone just mentioned turns up
a speech about Old Nick, the Devil

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when someone being discussed appears, and literally means discussing Satan.

clue.text: Aim to exploit first early-morning rail service

indicators.note: first places the exploiting word ahead of the aiming word

parts.note: to milk is to exploit for gain
to aim a weapon is to train it

explanation.surface: Someone plans to take advantage of an opportunity before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: A British early train that once carried churns of milk, stopping everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a slow early train that carried milk churns, now any very early service.

clue.text: Film about love is a bit wet

indicators.note: the film word goes around the love letter

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, like a mist on glass
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a romantic film as rather soppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' looks like a jibe meaning feeble; it is literal dampness.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly damp, which is what a bit wet describes.

clue.text: A section of the Circle Line

definitions.text: A section of the Circle Line

parts.words: A section of the Circle Line
parts.note: a portion of the curved line round a geometric circle, dressed up as London's Underground route

explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it is the circumference of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry, a curved portion of a circle's circumference is this.

clue.text: Get thick mud on shoe at end of village merrymaking

parts.note: to cake is to cover thickly with dried mud
a sandal is a kind of shoe

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A villager's footwear gets muddy during a country festival.
explanation.walkthrough: A literary phrase for revelry, from Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means carefree pleasure and festivity, which merrymaking also means.

clue.text: Feature of sculpture that's outstanding

parts.note: carving in which figures project from a flat background, punning on outstanding as excellent

explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' suggests excellent; it means literally standing out from the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In sculpture, raised carving that projects from a background is so called.

clue.text: Supporting bar, I built up energy with new drug

indicators.note: in a down entry, built up means written upwards, so the run is turned backwards

parts.note: supporting means for, as in in favour of
a pub is a bar
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A gym-goer at the bar builds strength and then takes a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built up' reverses FOR, PUB and I together to give IBUPROF.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common anti-inflammatory painkiller, an example of a drug.

clue.text: When heavy metal hits began?

parts.note: the prehistoric era when a dense metal came into use, dressed up as a question about rock music

explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal hits' suggests rock music; it is the metal used for tools and weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period when iron tools came into use followed the Bronze Age.

clue.text: Rising, about to occupy a post with soldier

indicators.note: the about letter occupies the middle of the post word

parts.note: to post is to send
C is circa, Latin for about
a soldier ant is a worker in an ant colony

explanation.surface: A soldier is promoted, taking up a new posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' in crosswords often means ANT, from the soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendant means rising, especially in power or in astrology.

clue.text: Poetic Indian greeting, a prelude to activity — what's funny in that?

indicators.note: the shuffled word goes into the run just built

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: the prelude to a word is its first letter
funny means odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word what, with 's for is as a link

explanation.surface: Someone greets a famous poetic hero and asks what is amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a prelude to activity' supplies two A pieces: the word 'a' itself and the first letter of activity. 'in that' puts the shuffle inside the run of greeting and those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of Longfellow's narrative poem is a Native American.

clue.text: Kicked out of play, but maintaining contact

definitions.meaning: in rugby or football, the ball crossing the sideline

explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the touch is the area beyond the sidelines; the idiom also means staying in contact.

clue.text: Grand city always rejected the country

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the whole run is reversed

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A grand city that has always been rejected by the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'rejected', turns both city and always together; e'er is poetic for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a country in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Wrongly-spelt — noun ' one's found in agreement

indicators.note: one's letters are found inside the shuffled word
wrongly spelt means the letters are in the wrong order

parts.note: one is I, and the 's stands for is, giving IS

explanation.surface: A grammarian finds a misspelt noun.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe and dash are printing faults. 'one's' is read as one is, so I plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting together in harmony, which is agreement.

clue.text: Less extreme novel? Editor pushes the boat out

indicators.note: the editor pushes the boat aside, taking its place
out shows the boat word leaves the novel's title

parts.note: Watership Down is Richard Adams's novel about rabbits

explanation.surface: An editor spends lavishly on a new novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pushes the boat out' is a British idiom for spending lavishly; here ED replaces SHIP (the boat) in WATERSHIP DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Watered down means diluted, made less extreme or forceful.

clue.text: Beaten by a second?

parts.note: a race result where one finisher was beaten by the runner-up, not by a split second of time

explanation.walkthrough: 'a second' suggests a fraction of time; it is the person in second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The finisher in bronze position is beaten by the runner-up in second place.

clue.text: Vessel turned up laden with gold in island republic

indicators.note: the vessel is loaded with the gold, which goes inside
in a down entry, turned up means written upwards

parts.note: an urn is a vessel
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An upturned vase full of gold is found on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laden with' suggests carrying cargo; here the gold symbol is loaded inside the upturned vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny Pacific island nation and a republic.

clue.text: Grandmother baked bread

definitions.meaning: an informal name for a granny
a flat leavened bread from South Asia

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a familiar word for granny and an Indian flatbread baked in a tandoor.

clue.text: One taking in some illegal, activity

definitions.text: One taking in some illegal, activity

parts.words: One taking in some illegal, activity
parts.note: someone who takes things as part of a crime

explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' suggests absorbing; it is taking as stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who steals takes property, which is criminal activity.

clue.text: Start on plonk during Sunday, drunk by six, given this?

definitions.text: Start on plonk during Sunday, drunk by six, given this?

indicators.note: by means next to, so six sits beside the rest

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the plonk letter comes during the Sunday letters
drunk means the letters stagger into a new order
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone drinking plonk on a Sunday might be drunk by six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges SUNDAY to NDUAYS; P goes inside after U. The whole clue also describes the cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: French country wine is cheap table wine, the plonk that could leave one drunk by evening.

clue.text: Perhaps reading in Tyndale's translation with enthusiasm

indicators.note: the reading letter goes in the reworked name
a translation turns words into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: William Tyndale, translator of the Bible into English
reading is one of the three Rs, so it may be R

explanation.surface: Someone reads Tyndale's English Bible translation with zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals an example: reading is one of the three Rs. 'translation' rearranges TYNDALE to ADENTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardently means passionately or eagerly, with enthusiasm.

clue.text: One may invite: the press to function — not back to bar

definitions.text: One may invite: the press to function

indicators.note: to means joined on, so the reversed word attaches to the bar word

parts.note: but means except, as does bar

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A device invites the press to attend a function, but not a drinks bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like journalists; it means pushing.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is pressed to make a machine work, inviting a press to operate.
